verdict.reasoning: No single work covers all four components, so SCOOPED is off the table: no hit combines (a) as worded — a postcondition/subgoal-success probe on the frozen VLA's OWN internal features — with (b) a scripted physical retreat-and-reattempt. ProbeAct's probe is geometric (object 3D positions) and its recovery is a continuous CBF filter; HELM's verifier is an external MLP over observation/action/subgoal/memory context, not VLA internals; Agentic Robot's verifier is an external fine-tuned VLM. However, the field brackets the claim from both sides, and the verified evidence makes the residual delta thin. HELM (abstract fetched and confirmed via Semantic Scholar; the searcher input contained one confessed hallucination so single-source kills were verified) already delivers a learned failure verifier + physical rollback-and-replan recovery + LIBERO-Long + explicit same-budget comparison + a quantified three-gap failure breakdown (41% memory / 33% verification / 26% recovery), plus releases LIBERO-Recovery infrastructure — it lacks only the internal-feature probe. ProbeAct already delivers probe-on-frozen-internals triggering autonomous online correction on a LIBERO variant. Agentic Robot already delivers verifier-triggered scripted recovery (gripper lift + retry) on LIBERO-Long. VLA-Corrector (also verified) delivers a frozen-backbone latent monitor + triggered corrective replanning + LIBERO + call-efficiency accounting. Every pairwise combination of the four axes exists; only the exact four-way conjunction is open, and its defensibility for RA-L/TMLR depends on execution: the paper MUST run budget-matched head-to-heads against an external-verifier trigger (HELM/Agentic-Robot-style) and a continuous-correction baseline (ProbeAct-style), must use or engage HELM's LIBERO-Recovery protocol, and must distinguish its taxonomy from HELM's gap breakdown and ReViP's false-completion benchmark suite. Without those comparisons reviewers will read the work as a recombination of published parts. The claim survives only with the narrowed wording below; do not claim novelty for any individual component — (a) alone is established (SAFE, AEGIS, What-Frozen-VLAs-Know, VLAConf, VLA-FAIL), verifier-triggered recovery on LIBERO is established (HELM, Agentic Robot, B2FF), quantified failure taxonomies are established (HELM, RoboFail, benchmarking papers), and budget-matched accounting is established (HELM, AEGIS, FAR).
verdict.surviving_delta: To our knowledge, this is the first system in which a learned subgoal-postcondition probe reading a frozen VLA's own internal features — rather than an external VLM, an observation-level verifier (HELM, Agentic Robot), or a geometric object-position probe (ProbeAct) — directly triggers an autonomous scripted retreat-and-reattempt recovery, evaluated on LIBERO-Long under matched timestep budgets against both external-verifier-triggered and continuous-correction baselines, together with a quantified taxonomy of silent postcondition violations.

hits.paper: ProbeAct: Probe-Guided Training-Free Failure Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: Trains a lightweight multi-target hidden-state probe on a frozen VLA (predicts 3D positions of task-relevant objects from intermediate features) to detect grasp/transport/placement failures, then corrects actions via a hierarchical Control Barrier Function filter that encodes repeated-failure locations as soft safe-set constraints. Evaluated on LIBERO-plus, improves OpenVLA-OFT from 69.6%->74.1%.
hits.overlap_assessment: Covers (a) fully -- probe on frozen VLA's own internal features, not external VLM. Covers (c) partially -- LIBERO-plus but no explicit matched-timestep-budget accounting confirmed. Does NOT cover (b) -- correction is continuous CBF-based action steering, not a scripted discrete physical retreat-and-reattempt. Does NOT cover (d) -- no formal quantified taxonomy of silent postcondition violations, only named failure categories in passing. Closest single paper on the (a) premise; the mechanism for (b) is a different design choice (soft constraint vs. scripted retreat) that a paper could legitimately argue against.

hits.what_it_does: For diffusion policies (not VLAs): trains its own IQL-style critic to identify failure-inducing actions, retries by resetting to initial configuration, and performs 5-10 gradient steps of test-time adaptation on the policy itself; evaluated on ManiSkill/RoboSuite/RoboMimic with timestep-budget-matched success-rate comparisons.
hits.overlap_assessment: Retreat-to-initial-configuration + retry loop (b-like) with timestep-budget accounting methodology (c-like practice) — but requires backbone gradient updates (explicitly finetunes the policy at test time), is not a VLA, not evaluated on LIBERO, and the failure signal comes from a separately-trained critic, not a probe on frozen VLA features. Adjacent on methodology (budget-matched retry evaluation) but wrong model class and violates the frozen-backbone premise.

hits.paper: AEGIS: A Backup Reflex for Physical AI
hits.what_it_does: Trains a lightweight probe on a weak policy's FROZEN activations to detect high-risk steps early, then escalates control to a stronger separate policy for just those steps. Evaluated on LIBERO-Spatial with rigorous budget-matched comparisons (blind escalation, random-trigger placebo controls at the same 38% activation budget), pre-registered analysis plan, McNemar tests. AEGIS recovers 10.1% of trajectories the weak policy loses vs 4.6%/5.1% for budget-matched controls.
hits.overlap_assessment: Strong match on (a)-style mechanism (probe on frozen policy activations predicting failure) and a genuine matched-budget evaluation methodology (close cousin of (c)'s 'matched-timestep-budget accounting', though the match is compute-budget not timestep-budget and on LIBERO-Spatial not long-horizon LIBERO-Long). Does NOT match (b): recovery is policy-switching/escalation to a stronger policy, not a scripted physical retreat-and-reattempt. Explicitly excludes LIBERO-Long from main runs ('pre-registration named LIBERO-Long ... as candidate long-horizon suites' but excluded for being 'out of the weak-failure window'), so (c)'s long-horizon requirement is not met. No taxonomy of silent postcondition violations (d) — confirmed via full-text check: 'postcondition'/'subgoal' terms do not appear, no quantified failure taxonomy.

hits.paper: ProbeAct: Probe-Guided Training-Free Failure Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: Lightweight multi-target hidden-state probe on frozen VLA features predicting 3D positions of task-relevant objects, combined with a Control Barrier Function (CBF) filter that minimally corrects actions in real time. Raises OpenVLA-OFT success on LIBERO-plus from 69.6% to 74.1%. Defines qualitative failure categories (hard/soft empty grasp, mid-transport drop) via gripper-width/end-effector heuristics.
hits.overlap_assessment: Matches (a) reasonably (probe on frozen VLA hidden states) though the probe predicts object geometry rather than postcondition/subgoal success directly. Does NOT match (b): recovery is a continuous CBF action-correction filter, not a scripted physical retreat-and-reattempt — confirmed via full text (no discrete retreat maneuver, just per-step action projection). Failure categories are named but NOT quantified with counts/frequencies (partial d at best — 'no frequency statistics are provided'). Timestep-budget accounting is confounded, not matched: baseline failed episodes consume the full 600-step timeout while rescued episodes average 197 steps, so это not a clean matched-budget design per (c). LIBERO-plus, not confirmed as long-horizon-specific.

hits.paper: SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: Foundational multitask failure detector: learns from VLA internal features (OpenVLA, π0, π0-FAST) to predict a single scalar failure-likelihood, trained on successful+failed rollouts, evaluated for generalization to unseen tasks in sim and real, using conformal prediction for the accuracy/detection-time tradeoff.
hits.overlap_assessment: Cleanest single match to leg (a) alone (probe reading a frozen VLA's own internal features, not an external VLM/detector) — near-certainly already known to the project as the seminal work in this line. Does NOT implement any recovery/retry mechanism itself (abstract only motivates that a detector 'allows the robot to stop, backtrack, or ask for help' — no scripted retreat implemented); no LIBERO-long-horizon-specific matched-budget evaluation confirmed; no taxonomy of silent postcondition violations. Must be cited as prior art for (a) regardless of overlap on (b)-(d).

hits.paper: HELM: Harness-Enhanced Long-horizon Memory for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
hits.what_it_does: Model-agnostic execution harness with three parts: Episodic Memory Module (CLIP-indexed keyframes), a learned State Verifier (SV, a 3-layer MLP over observation+action+subgoal+memory context, NOT reading the VLA's own frozen hidden activations) that predicts action failure pre-execution, and a Harness Controller that performs rollback (retrieve last checkpoint, issue goal-conditioned 'return to the state shown' recovery sequence) and replanning. On LIBERO-LONG: 58.4%→81.5% success over OpenVLA, with an explicit same-rollout-budget comparison against LoRA adaptation ('OpenVLA+LoRA(50K) uses the same rollout budget as SV training, enabling a fair same-budget comparison'). Releases LIBERO-Recovery, a perturbation-injection protocol for evaluating recovery. Full-text failure breakdown: of 83 failed episodes, 41% memory-gap, 33% verification-gap, 26% recovery-gap failures (18% multi-mode).
hits.overlap_assessment: Closest single-paper combination found: strong match to (c) (LIBERO-LONG specifically, WITH an explicit matched-budget comparison against a baseline) and to (d) (a quantified failure-mode taxonomy with percentages, though framed as memory/verification/recovery 'gaps' rather than 'silent postcondition violations' per se). Partial match to (b): the Harness Controller's rollback is a genuine physical return-to-a-prior-state maneuver, but it is goal-conditioned/generative ('issue a goal-conditioned recovery sequence') rather than a hard-coded SCRIPTED retreat. Does NOT match (a) as specified: the State Verifier is an externally-trained MLP over observation/action/subgoal/memory context, not a probe reading the frozen VLA's own internal features — closer to the claim's excluded 'SuccessVQA-style success detection' category. Also introduces LIBERO-Recovery as public infrastructure, which is directly relevant prior art regardless of citation outcome. This is the single strongest threat to the claim's residual novelty and should be read in full, not just abstract.

hits.paper: Back to the Familiar Future (B2FF): Failure Recovery for VLA Policies via Pre-Imagined Milestone Selection
hits.what_it_does: Generates a bank of 'familiar future' milestone images from the clean initial observation before execution; at recovery time a recoverability-aware selector picks a milestone and enforces it as a fixed visual goal. On failure-injected LIBERO, raises a baseline VLA from 56.3% to 74.0%. Recovery entry uses either the known injected-perturbation timestep or a human-annotated failure-onset point (Standard LIBERO).
hits.overlap_assessment: Does not match (a): no probe on frozen internal features — uses pre-generated goal images, and recovery-entry detection in 'Standard LIBERO' relies on human annotation, not a learned violation detector. Does not match (b): recovery enforces a generated visual goal, not a scripted physical retreat-and-reattempt. Partial match to (c): failure-injected LIBERO, but budget-matching not confirmed. No taxonomy (d).

hits.paper: Foresight: Failure Detection for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Action-Conditioned World Model Latents
hits.what_it_does: Failure detector using latent representations from a separate action-conditioned world model (not the VLA's own frozen features), trained only on final task-level success/failure labels, calibrated via functional conformal prediction. Evaluated on LIBERO-Long, ManiSkill-Long, and BEHAVIOR-1K plus real robots.
hits.overlap_assessment: Strong match on the benchmark half of (c) (LIBERO-Long specifically, long-horizon), but the detector reads a separate world-model's latents, not the frozen VLA's own internal features, so (a) is not met as specified. No recovery mechanism (b). No taxonomy of silent postcondition violations confirmed (d). Detection-only paper; relevant as a strong 'detection on LIBERO-Long' precedent to cite and distinguish from.

hits.paper: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
hits.what_it_does: Training-free safeguard for action-chunked policies: a zero-shot failure detector (Temporal Inter-chunk Discrepancy Estimate, self-consistency across overlapping action chunks, calibrated with split conformal prediction) combined with state-respawning that rewinds execution to the latest VLM-identified (offline) semantically-verified safe checkpoint, using a frozen policy encoder to build the checkpoint feature database.
hits.overlap_assessment: Partial match to (a): uses a frozen policy encoder for checkpoint features, but the online detector itself is a self-consistency signal (TIDE) rather than a trained postcondition/success probe, and checkpoint identification is done offline by an external VLM — violating the 'not an external VLM/detector' condition. Partial match to (b): 'state-respawning' rewinds to a prior state, conceptually retreat-like, but is a learned/semantic rewind to a stored checkpoint rather than a scripted physical retreat maneuver. Long-horizon manipulation tasks used but LIBERO-specific matched-budget accounting not confirmed. No taxonomy (d).

hits.paper: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: Two lightweight failure detectors requiring no failure data: last-layer Mahalanobis distance (LLMD) on frozen last-layer VLA features for OOD detection, and action-chunk-consistency (ACC) exploiting receding-horizon overlap. Introduces AUCPDT metric jointly capturing precision/recall/detection-time.
hits.overlap_assessment: Solid match to (a) (probe/statistical detector directly on frozen VLA's own last-layer features). No recovery mechanism (b). Benchmark not confirmed as LIBERO long-horizon specifically, no matched-budget accounting confirmed (c), no taxonomy (d). Cite as prior art for the detection-only half of the claim.

hits.paper: What Frozen VLAs Already Know About Success: A Probing Study of Value-Like Structure in Foundation Robot Policies
hits.what_it_does: Pure probing study: linear probes on frozen OpenVLA/Pi0.5/DINOv2/CLIP features recover Monte-Carlo success/outcome targets from LIBERO-Goal rollouts (~92% pairwise ordering accuracy for Pi0.5, controlled for task/temporal shortcuts). Used as a test-time selector over sampled action prefixes, raising push-plate success from 26.7% to 44.3%.
hits.overlap_assessment: Direct methodological match to (a) — this is essentially the canonical 'learned probe on a frozen VLA's own internal features predicting success' result the claim's (a) describes, on LIBERO-Goal (not long-horizon). No recovery/retreat mechanism (b) — uses resampling/selection among candidate action prefixes, not physical retreat. Not long-horizon, no matched-budget framing, no taxonomy (c,d absent). Must be cited as the closest prior demonstration that frozen-VLA probes carry success-relevant signal, which the claim's (a) builds directly on top of.

hits.paper: How Visible Are Silent Manipulation Failures? An Observability Study of False-Success Detection in Simulated Robot Episodes
hits.what_it_does: Studies false-success episodes (robot logs success but task outcome was wrong) on two bimanual ALOHA tasks (cube transfer, peg insertion), comparing how much of the information needed to overturn a false-success label is recoverable from proprioception alone vs requiring vision.
hits.overlap_assessment: Directly relevant to the 'silent postcondition violation' framing in (d) by name/theme, but provides no quantified taxonomy of violation TYPES (only a recoverability analysis of one failure category — false success), no probe-on-frozen-VLA-features mechanism, no recovery/retry, and no LIBERO or long-horizon evaluation. Cite for terminology/framing precedent on 'silent' failures, but does not overlap the actual (a)-(c) mechanisms.

hits.paper: RePO-VLA: Recovery-Driven Policy Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: Trains a policy (Recovery-Aware Initialization + Progress-Aware Semantic Value Function + Value-Conditioned Refinement) to prefer high-progress actions, explicitly replacing online failure detectors/heuristic retries with a fixed high-value bias baked into the policy via training. Introduces FRBench, a recovery-focused benchmark with standardized error injection.
hits.overlap_assessment: Explicitly the opposite design point from the claim: '(recovery) at deployment ... without online failure detectors or heuristic retries' — this is a finetuning/policy-optimization recipe (likely requires backbone gradients, which would also put it out of scope per this project's frozen-backbone constraint), not a frozen-backbone probe+scripted-retry system. Low direct overlap with (a)/(b), but FRBench is a relevant recovery-evaluation benchmark to be aware of for (c)-adjacent framing.

hits.paper: VeriSpace: Spatially Grounded Action Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models
hits.what_it_does: 3D-aware external action verifier that scores candidate actions via scene encoding (visual+3D geometry) and spatially-grounded reasoning, used for test-time action selection among multiple VLA-proposed candidates.
hits.overlap_assessment: Explicitly an external verifier (its own encoder/reasoning module), not a probe on the frozen VLA's own internal features — fails (a) by the claim's own exclusion criterion. No scripted retreat-and-reattempt (b). Benchmark and budget-matching not confirmed as LIBERO long-horizon. Low overlap, adjacent to the 'external VLM/detector' category the claim already excludes.

hits.what_it_does: Trains lightweight LINEAR PROBES on FROZEN VLA internal features (OpenVLA, Pi0.5, DINOv2, CLIP) to recover Monte-Carlo success/outcome targets from mixed successful+failed manipulation trajectories on LIBERO-Goal. Verified via direct abstract fetch (not just AI summary): probes reach ~92% pairwise ordering accuracy under same-task/same-timestep controls; used as a test-time selector over sampled Pi0.5 action prefixes, raising push-plate success 26.7%->44.3%.

hits.paper: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
hits.what_it_does: Training-free online safeguard: TIDE failure detector monitors the policy's own internal self-consistency (disagreement between overlapping predicted action chunks in the temporal ensembler -- i.e., reads the policy's own internal state, not an external VLM). On detection, a 'state-respawning' mechanism has the robot PHYSICALLY execute a recovery action to steer back toward a previously-verified good state, then clears stale policy memory. Evaluated on 6 real-world bimanual tasks + RoboCasa sim (20-50 rollouts/task).
hits.overlap_assessment: Covers (a) [detector reads the policy's own internal consistency signal, arguably 'frozen internal features'] and (b) [physical steer-back-and-resume is functionally close to scripted retreat-and-reattempt] together in one system. Does NOT cover (c): evaluated on RoboCasa + real-world, explicitly NOT LIBERO, and no timestep-budget accounting reported. Does NOT cover (d): only qualitative failure examples (dropped objects, misaligned placements), no quantified taxonomy. This is the strongest (a)+(b) combination found across all searches -- the delta for the target claim rests entirely on porting this combination to LIBERO-class long-horizon with budget accounting plus adding the taxonomy.

hits.overlap_assessment: Covers (a) [frozen-feature probe] and (c) [LIBERO]. Explicitly does NOT implement any triggered recovery -- 'the robot can stop, backtrack, or ask for help' is offered only as an unimplemented suggestion, not (b). hits.overlap_assessment: Covers (a) [frozen-feature-based OOD/failure detection]. No recovery mechanism found (no (b)), benchmark/LIBERO use and taxonomy not confirmed in available text (likely not (c)/(d) as a combination). Must-cite as a closely related frozen-feature failure-detection method.
